description: Queries where contexts contain conflicting information - system should mark as DISPUTED

contexts: The project launch was a complete success. All systems performed as expected and user adoption exceeded targets by 40%.
The project launch failed catastrophically. Critical bugs caused system outages affecting thousands of users.
The company reported record profits of $2.3 billion in 2024, marking its fifth consecutive year of growth.
The company posted a net loss of $450 million in 2024, forcing layoffs of 15% of its workforce.

cases.query: Was the medication approved by the FDA?
contexts: The FDA granted full approval for the medication in March 2024, citing strong efficacy data from Phase 3 trials.
The FDA rejected the medication's application in March 2024 due to insufficient safety data and concerns about side effects.
Sales increased 25% quarter-over-quarter, driven by strong demand in the Asian market.
Sales declined 18% compared to last quarter as supply chain issues impacted product availability.

cases.query: What is the effectiveness rate of the vaccine?
contexts: Clinical trials conducted by Pfizer showed the vaccine was 95% effective at preventing symptomatic infection.
Real-world data from Israel found the vaccine was only 64% effective against the Delta variant.
A UK study reported 88% effectiveness against hospitalization.
cases.rationale: Numerical disagreement across different studies (95% vs 64% vs 88%)

cases.query: When was the Great Wall of China built?
contexts: The Great Wall was primarily built during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644), with most existing sections dating to this period.
Construction of the Great Wall began during the Qin Dynasty under Emperor Qin Shi Huang around 221 BC.
Archaeological evidence suggests wall-building in China dates back to the 7th century BC, predating unified China.
cases.description: Different historical accounts giving different time periods
cases.rationale: Different historical accounts giving different time periods

contexts: The asteroid impact theory, supported by the Chicxulub crater, is now the scientific consensus for dinosaur extinction.
Volcanic activity from the Deccan Traps in India released massive amounts of gases, causing climate change that killed the dinosaurs.
Some scientists argue it was a combination of asteroid impact and volcanic activity that led to the mass extinction.
cases.description: Competing scientific theories for the same event
cases.rationale: Competing scientific theories for the same event

cases.query: How many people died in the Titanic sinking?
contexts: The official British inquiry concluded that 1,503 people died when the Titanic sank on April 15, 1912.
The US Senate investigation put the death toll at 1,517, based on different passenger manifest interpretations.
Recent historical analysis suggests the actual number may be closer to 1,496, accounting for name duplications in records.
cases.description: Different authoritative sources give different numbers
cases.rationale: Different authoritative sources give different numbers

cases.query: Is remote work more productive than office work?
contexts: A Stanford study found remote workers were 13% more productive, with fewer breaks and sick days.
Microsoft research showed that while individual productivity increased, collaboration and innovation suffered in remote settings.
A Harvard study found productivity varied significantly by role - creative work suffered while routine tasks improved.
Managers reported difficulty assessing remote worker productivity, leading to potential measurement biases in all studies.
cases.description: Nuanced disagreement - studies show different aspects
cases.rationale: Nuanced disagreement - studies show different aspects, no clear answer

cases.query: Is coffee good for your health?
contexts: Research published in NEJM found that coffee drinkers had a 10-15% lower risk of death from heart disease and diabetes.
Studies show coffee can increase anxiety, disrupt sleep patterns, and raise blood pressure in sensitive individuals.
The health effects of coffee depend heavily on individual genetics, particularly the CYP1A2 gene that affects caffeine metabolism.
Pregnant women are advised to limit coffee intake due to potential risks to fetal development.
cases.rationale: Context-dependent and conflicting evidence - benefits and risks both exist
